callees.name: local_backend_toml_updates
callees.signature: local_backend_toml_updates(env_path: Path, backend: str) -> dict[str, Any]
callees.pre_condition: env_path is a Path that identifies a readable .env file or does not identify an existing file. backend is a non-empty string that is not 'opencode'.
callees.post_condition: Returns a non-empty dict mapping dot-separated TOML field paths within the LLM section to new values along a key path that sets the LLM backend to backend. When model or effort values exist in the project .env or fm-agent.toml configuration, their current values are preserved in the returned dict.

callees.name: update_llm_settings_toml_text
callees.signature: update_llm_settings_toml_text(toml_text: str, updates: dict[str, Any]) -> str
callees.pre_condition: toml_text is valid TOML text. updates is a non-empty dict whose keys are dot-separated field paths that each resolve to a writable leaf location in the LLM section of toml_text.
callees.post_condition: Returns valid TOML text in which every field path present in updates has been set to its corresponding value and all other content of toml_text is unchanged.

callees.name: remove_legacy_llm_env_overrides
callees.signature: remove_legacy_llm_env_overrides(env_text: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, tuple[str, ...]]
callees.pre_condition: env_text is the text content of a .env file or None.
callees.post_condition: Returns (updated_env, removed_overrides). removed_overrides is a tuple of environment variable names whose legacy LLM override entries were present in env_text before the call and are absent from updated_env; every other entry from the original env_text is preserved unchanged in updated_env. When env_text is None or empty, returns (env_text, ()).

callees.name: backup_file
callees.pre_condition: path identifies an existing readable file.
callees.post_condition: Returns a Path to a copy of the file at path whose content is byte-for-byte identical to the content path held at the time of the call.

callees.name: atomic_write
callees.pre_condition: path is a writable filesystem path.
callees.post_condition: Upon return, path contains exactly content. The write is atomic: any concurrent reader of path observes either the complete prior content or the complete new content.
